function: Estimation of the deterministic BS-IRS-user cascaded channel (via its covariance, up to a phase) at selected grids from average received power measurements under random IRS reflections (pp. 13-17).
system: Single-antenna-equivalent BS and users, passive reflecting IRS with 8x8 elements and 1- or 2-bit phase shifts, direct link blocked, narrowband, band not stated (pp. 5, 9, 18).
method: Single-layer NN (2 neurons, 2N+1 weights) trained per grid by SGD/backpropagation on an MSE loss over power measurements; non-learned variogram grid selection and SDP-based reflection design (pp. 14-17, 19).
data_channel: Ray-tracing channels of a real-world 30 m x 30 m region in London (10x10 grids of 3 m); no named ray-tracing tool or dataset (p. 18).
test_conditions: Trained per grid on its power measurements, with a held-out validation part; swept noise power, M2, Q, phase-shift bits; no unseen scenario (pp. 16-20).
baselines: Non-learned: CSM/ACSM and random-max sampling (power-measurement IRS designs); perfect-CSI upper bound; uniform and random location selection; no earlier learned method compared (pp. 19-22).
metrics: NMSE of the estimated channel covariance (Fig. 6); average received SNR versus number of reflection sets and number of selected grids (Figs. 7, 9) (pp. 18-22).
complexity: O(N) training complexity per grid (2 neurons, 2N+1 weights); NN-SR linear and NN-GAR polynomial in N for reflection design (pp. 17, 20).
openness: none; no code or data link given; simulation uses a ray-tracing channel of a London region without naming a dataset (p. 18).
q1_support: p. 18: "We focus on a real-world simulation setup, i.e., a square subregion in London" - ray-tracing channel of a London region with no named tool, 3GPP model, public dataset or measurement; the model of p. 6 is a generic geometric model plus Gaussian random paths.
q2_support: p. 16: "we can make full use of the power measurements" - the NN is trained per grid on its own measurements and validated on a held-out part of them; sweeps over noise, M2, Q and phase bits are retrained; no unseen scenario is tested.
q3_support: p. 19: "we adopt the CSM [23], [24] and random-max sampling (RMS) [23], [38] methods as benchmark schemes" - only non-learned power-measurement baselines and a perfect-CSI bound; no earlier learned method is evaluated.
q4_support: p. 17: "the number of weights is 2N + 1, which incurs the computational complexity for each grid in the order of O(N)" - order of complexity of the NN training.
q5_support: p. 18: "We focus on a real-world simulation setup, i.e., a square subregion in London" - authors' own simulation; no code or data link, no public dataset and no measured data.
notes: PDF is the arXiv v1 preprint (2405.12432v1, 21 May 2024; p. 1). Borderline for no_learning but included: the estimator is a single-layer NN trained by SGD and backpropagation on measured power with a validation split (pp. 15-17), yet its weights are the channel, it is trained per grid, and the reflection design is non-learned (p. 19). Area 2 because the learned part is channel estimation; the final metric is coverage SNR, so the reviewer may prefer area 3. RIS present, so the single-antenna exclusion does not apply.
